about: Batch 04, slice A, chunk A30: lunches (pitas, wraps, panini, rice and lentil bowls, savoury pastries, hot sandwiches) from Turkey, Greece, the Middle East, Italy, India, the Caribbean, Mexico, Spain, Scandinavia and the US.

recipes.title: Peynirli Ispanakli Pide (Turkish Spinach and Feta Flatbread)
recipes.summary: A boat-shaped flatbread baked with spinach, feta and an egg in the middle, a bakery lunch from Turkey.
steps: Heat the oven to 230°C (210°C fan). Cut the base in half and roll each piece into an oval, pinching the long edges up to make a rim.
Soften the spinach and onion in the oil in a pan for 3 minutes until the spinach wilts, then cool slightly and mix with the crumbled feta.
Fill the boats and bake for 10 minutes, until the edges are golden.
Crack an egg into the middle of each, sprinkle with chilli and bake for 3 more minutes, until the white is set.
notes: Food safety: the egg white must be set right through. Keeps 2 days in the fridge; reheat until steaming hot.
Contains egg, milk and gluten.

recipes.title: Pork Souvlaki Pitas (with Tzatziki)
recipes.summary: Lemon and oregano pork skewers pan-seared and wrapped in warm pita with tzatziki, tomato and onion.
steps: Toss the pork with the oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano and 1 tsp salt.
Thread onto skewers or leave loose and cook in a hot pan for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through to 70°C with no pink inside.
Warm the pitas, spread with tzatziki and fill with the pork, tomato and onion.
notes: Food safety: pork must be cooked through with no pink. Cool leftovers within an hour; for a packed lunch pack the meat chilled with an ice pack, eat within 4 hours and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk and gluten.

recipes.title: Greek Chicken Gyro Pitas (with Red Onion)
recipes.summary: Oregano and lemon chicken thigh seared until charred, tucked into warm pita with tzatziki, tomato and red onion.
steps: Toss the chicken with the oil, lemon juice, oregano, paprika, garlic and 1 tsp salt.
Cook in a hot frying pan in two batches for 6 minutes each, until charred in places and cooked through to 75°C.
Warm the pitas and fill with tzatziki, chicken, tomato and onion.
notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour; for a packed lunch use an ice pack, eat within 4 hours and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains milk and gluten.

recipes.title: Spiced Lamb and Hummus Bowl (with Pita)
recipes.summary: Cumin-spiced lamb mince over a swirl of hummus with cucumber, tomato and parsley, scooped up with warm pita.
steps: Brown the lamb in the oil over high heat for 8 minutes, breaking it up, with the spices and salt, until cooked through to 75°C.
Spread the hummus in four bowls and top with the lamb.
Add the cucumber, tomato and parsley and serve with the warmed pita.
notes: Food safety: lamb mince must reach 75°C with no pink. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot; for a packed lunch keep the lamb and hummus below 5°C with an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.
Contains gluten and sesame.

recipes.title: Tuna Nicoise Bowl (with Potato and Green Beans)
recipes.summary: Tinned tuna, boiled egg, potato, beans and olives with a mustard dressing, a lunch bowl that holds up in a lunchbox.
steps: Boil the potatoes for 12 minutes, adding the beans for the last 3 minutes, until the potatoes are tender. Drain.
Boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool in cold water, peel and halve.
Whisk the oil, lemon juice and mustard with salt and pepper.
Arrange the potatoes, beans, tuna, tomato, olives and eggs in two boxes and pour over the dressing.
notes: Food safety: tuna, egg and potatoes must stay below 5°C. For a packed lunch use an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.
Contains egg and fish.

recipes.title: Quinoa and Chickpea Lunch Bowl (with Feta)
recipes.summary: Fluffy quinoa, chickpeas, cucumber, tomato and feta in a lemon dressing that keeps well in the fridge.
steps: Rinse the quinoa, simmer in the water for 15 minutes, until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender, then cool.
Toss with the chickpeas, cucumber, tomato, feta and parsley.
Dress with the oil, lemon juice and salt and pepper.
notes: Keeps 3 days in a sealed container in the fridge. For a packed lunch use an ice pack.
Contains milk.

recipes.title: Caprese Panini (with Pesto)
recipes.summary: Pressed crusty bread with melting mozzarella, ripe tomato, basil and a spoon of pesto, crisp outside and gooey inside.
steps: Spread the pesto on both cut sides of the bread, then layer the mozzarella, tomato and basil on the base. Season and close.
Brush the outsides with the oil.
Press in a hot pan or sandwich press for 4 minutes each side, until golden and the cheese has melted.
notes: Pesto is traditionally made with a hard cheese; check the label if you need it vegetarian.
Contains milk, gluten and nuts.

recipes.title: Piadina Romagnola (with Prosciutto, Mozzarella and Rocket)
recipes.summary: A warm Italian flatbread folded around prosciutto, creamy mozzarella and peppery rocket, ready in 10 minutes.
steps: Warm each flatbread in a dry pan for 1 minute each side, until soft with a few brown spots.
Cover half of each with the mozzarella and warm for 1 minute until it just softens.
Add the prosciutto and rocket, drizzle with oil and fold over.
notes: Food safety: prosciutto and mozzarella should stay below 5°C until use. For a packed lunch use an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.
Contains gluten and milk.

recipes.title: Dal Tadka (with Ghee and Basmati Rice)
recipes.summary: Creamy red lentils finished with a sizzling ghee, cumin and garlic tempering, served over basmati rice.
steps: Simmer the lentils, water, turmeric, onion, tomato and 1 tsp salt for 20 minutes, until the lentils break down into a thick soup.
Cook the rice per the packet until tender, about 12 minutes.
Heat the ghee in a small pan, fry the cumin seeds and garlic for 1 minute until golden, add the chilli flakes and pour the tempering sizzling over the dal.
Serve the dal over the rice.
notes: Food safety: cool leftover rice within an hour; reheat once until steaming hot. The dal keeps 4 days in the fridge and freezes well.
Contains milk (ghee).

recipes.title: Paneer Kathi Rolls (with Mint Chutney)
recipes.summary: Spiced paneer, capsicum and onion rolled in warm flour tortillas with a smear of mint chutney, a Kolkata street classic.
steps: Fry the paneer in the oil over medium-high heat for 4 minutes, until golden on all sides.
Add the capsicum, onion and garam masala and cook for 4 minutes, until the vegetables soften. Squeeze over the lemon and season.
Warm the tortillas, spread with the chutney, fill with the paneer mixture and roll tightly.
notes: Keeps 1 day in the fridge wrapped in foil. For a packed lunch use an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.
Contains milk and gluten.

recipes.title: Vada Pav (Mumbai Spiced Potato Fritter in a Bread Roll)
recipes.summary: A garlicky spiced potato fritter in a soft bread roll with mint chutney, Mumbai's favourite hand-held lunch.
steps: Boil the potato for 15 minutes until tender, drain and mash roughly.
Fry the mustard seeds, curry leaves, garlic, chilli and turmeric in the first oil for 1 minute, then mix into the potato with 1 tsp salt. Shape into 8 patties.
Whisk the chickpea flour, water and a pinch of salt into a thick batter. Dip the patties and shallow fry in the second oil for 3 minutes each side, until deep golden.
Split the rolls, spread with chutney and fill with two fritters each.
notes: Best eaten hot. The potato mixture keeps 2 days in the fridge.
Contains gluten.

recipes.title: Lemon Rice (South Indian, with Peanuts and Curry Leaves)
recipes.summary: Turmeric-gold rice with a zesty lemon kick, crunchy peanuts and mustard seeds, a lunchbox favourite that eats well cold.
steps: Cook the rice per the packet until tender, about 12 minutes, then spread out to cool for 10 minutes.
Heat the oil, add the mustard seeds until they pop, then the curry leaves, peanuts and chilli for 2 minutes, until the peanuts are golden.
Stir in the turmeric, then toss through the rice with the lemon juice and 1 tsp salt.
notes: Food safety: rice must be cooled within an hour and kept below 5°C; eat within a day. For a packed lunch use an ice pack.
Contains peanuts.

recipes.title: Curd Rice (South Indian Yoghurt Rice with Cucumber)
recipes.summary: Cooling rice stirred with yoghurt, tempered with mustard seeds and curry leaves, with cucumber and pomegranate on top.
steps: Cook the rice in plenty of water for 15 minutes until very soft, drain and mash lightly. Cool for 10 minutes.
Stir through the yoghurt, milk and 1/2 tsp salt.
Heat the oil, add the mustard seeds until they pop, then the curry leaves and ginger for 30 seconds and pour over the rice.
Top with the cucumber and pomegranate.
notes: Food safety: cool the rice within an hour and keep below 5°C. For a packed lunch use an ice pack, eat within 4 hours and do not reheat.
Contains milk.

recipes.title: Egg Bhurji on Buttered Toast (Indian Spiced Scrambled Eggs)
recipes.summary: Soft scrambled eggs cooked with onion, tomato, chilli and turmeric, served on buttery toast in under 15 minutes.
steps: Soften the onion, chilli and tomato in half the butter for 4 minutes, until soft. Stir in the turmeric.
Add the beaten eggs and stir gently for 2 minutes, until just set but still creamy.
Toast and butter the bread until golden, then spoon the eggs on top. Sprinkle with coriander.
notes: Food safety: the eggs should be cooked until set, with no runny parts. Eat straight away.
Contains egg, milk and gluten.

recipes.title: Jamaican Beef Patties (Flaky Spiced Pastry Pockets)
recipes.summary: Flaky pastry pockets of curried, thyme-scented beef with a little scotch bonnet heat, perfect for the lunchbox.
steps: Brown the beef with the onion for 8 minutes, add the garlic, curry powder, thyme, allspice and scotch bonnet and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the water and breadcrumbs and simmer for 5 minutes, until thick. Season and cool completely.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Cut each pastry sheet into 3 rectangles, fill one half with the beef, fold over and crimp the edges with a fork.
Brush with the egg and bake for 20 minutes, until puffed and deep golden.
notes: Food safety: the beef must reach 75°C before it is cooled and filled, and the baked patties must be steaming hot in the middle. Cool within an hour; they keep 3 days in the fridge, and for a packed lunch use an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.
Contains egg and gluten.

recipes.title: Cuban Picadillo Bowl (with Rice, Olives and Raisins)
recipes.summary: Savoury-sweet beef simmered with tomato, olives and raisins, served over rice, a make-ahead lunch that reheats well.
steps: Cook the onion and capsicum in the oil for 5 minutes, add the beef and brown for 8 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains.
Stir in the garlic, spices, tomatoes, olives and raisins and simmer for 15 minutes, until thick and the beef reaches 75°C.
Meanwhile cook the rice per the packet until tender.
Serve the picadillo over the rice.
notes: Food safety: beef mince must reach 75°C. Cool within an hour; keeps 3 days in the fridge and freezes well. Reheat until steaming hot.
For a packed lunch use an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.

recipes.title: Meatball Subs (with Marinara and Melted Mozzarella)
recipes.summary: Tender beef meatballs in tangy marinara, piled into toasted rolls and grilled under melted mozzarella.
steps: Mix the mince, breadcrumbs, egg, garlic, oregano and 1 tsp salt and roll into 16 balls. Bake at 200°C (180°C fan) for 12 minutes, until browned.
Simmer the meatballs in the marinara for 10 minutes, until they reach 75°C in the centre.
Split the rolls, fill with meatballs and sauce, top with the cheese and grill for 3 minutes, until bubbling.
notes: Food safety: meatballs must reach 75°C with no pink. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains egg, milk and gluten.

recipes.title: Steak Sandwich (with Caramelised Onion and Rocket)
recipes.summary: Seared sirloin sliced over sweet onions, mustard mayo and rocket in a toasted crusty roll, a pub-style lunch.
steps: Cook the onion in half the oil over medium heat for 15 minutes, until soft and caramelised. Remove.
Season the steak and sear in the remaining oil for 3 minutes each side for medium, until browned with a core of 60°C. Rest for 5 minutes and slice thinly.
Toast the bread until crisp, spread with the mayonnaise and mustard and fill with the onions, steak and rocket.
notes: Food safety: whole steaks may be eaten medium once seared on the outside. For a packed lunch keep chilled with an ice pack and eat within 4 hours; cook the steak through if serving to anyone vulnerable.
Contains egg and gluten.

recipes.title: Chicken Club Sandwich (with Bacon and Tomato)
recipes.summary: A triple-decker of seared chicken, crisp bacon, tomato and lettuce with mayonnaise, a diner classic.
steps: Season the chicken and sear in the oil for 6 minutes each side, until cooked through to 75°C. Rest, then slice.
Cook the bacon in a dry pan for 6 minutes, until crisp.
Toast the bread until golden and spread with mayonnaise. Layer chicken, lettuce and tomato on two slices, add a second slice, then the bacon and the remaining slices.
Secure with picks, halve and serve.
notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C and bacon must be cooked right through. For a packed lunch keep chilled with an ice pack and eat within 4 hours.
Contains egg and gluten.

recipes.title: Open Prawn Smorrebrod (on Rye with Dill and Egg)
recipes.summary: Buttered rye topped with cooked prawns, egg, cucumber and dill mayonnaise, a Danish open sandwich.
steps: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes until hard, cool in cold water, peel and slice.
Mix the mayonnaise with half the dill and a squeeze of lemon.
Butter the rye, layer on the cucumber, egg and prawns until generously covered, and spoon over the mayonnaise. Finish with the remaining dill and lemon.
notes: Food safety: cooked prawns and egg must stay below 5°C; use within a day of cooking and eat within 4 hours at room temperature. For a packed lunch pack separately with an ice pack.
Contains crustacean, egg, milk and gluten.

recipes.title: Sloppy Joes (with Capsicum on Toasted Buns)
recipes.summary: Saucy, sweet-tangy beef mince with capsicum piled into toasted burger buns, a quick American lunch.
steps: Brown the beef with the onion and capsicum for 10 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains.
Add the garlic, paste, tomato sauce, Worcestershire, sugar, mustard and 1/4 cup water and simmer for 8 minutes, until thick and the beef reaches 75°C.
Toast the buns until golden and pile on the filling.
notes: Food safety: beef mince must reach 75°C. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour; for a packed lunch pack the filling in an insulated container, eat within 4 hours, or reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten, fish (Worcestershire) and milk may be in buns.
